clocks.overview: Logical sequence only. Column or row distance is not elapsed time; stage medians come from independent cohorts.
clocks.setup: One voice.setup event, origin t_connect_start. Mic permission/preparation is not fully covered by this timer.
clocks.avatar: One voice.avatar event, origin t_pc_created. total_ms starts at offer_start; differences of up to 1 ms are expected.
clocks.turn: One voice.turn event, origin t_speech_stopped by default; optional full speaking interval uses t_speech_started. Named *_ms fields retain original high-resolution derived durations; endpoints t_* are rounded independently.
clocks.judge: One backend clock: /answer start and duration lie within judge.call in the same operation. No alignment to browser monotonic offsets is claimed.
clocks.score: One backend request clock. 10/09 samples are distinct from the 10/10 voice sessions; no synthetic full-interview latency is produced.

statistics.stage_p50: Median of the named nonnegative duration field when available; setup adjacent intervals and transcript-to-click are differences within each event before median.
statistics.http_outside: median_i(Fetch_i - Server_i) = 263 ms. median(Fetch)=323; median(Server)=56; subtraction of these medians gives 267 ms and is a different statistic.
statistics.click_total: P50 of click_to_audible_ms = 1234 ms; sum of the five separate stage medians = 1217 ms. Never label the latter as an observed whole-turn median.
statistics.rtt: Compare same-interview WebRTC candidate-pair RTT windows with matched HTTP residuals, without claiming equal endpoints, instants, clocks or sample counts.

code_supported_dependencies: Microphone preparation and WebSocket opening run in parallel; recording requires micReady and session.updated.
Avatar starts after a session.updated frame supplies ICE servers; first read waits for media ready or the first-read timeout fallback.
Microphone upload and partial ASR output can overlap; no packet-level upload or ASR compute duration is reconstructed.
All seven observed final transcripts precede click; code also supports click then waiting for final transcript.
BANK /answer does not await Judge; stale Judge results can be discarded using draft/submit generation guards.
/answer completes before the next read request; response.created precedes first audible detection.
After final question: disconnect voice, review answers, user submits review, generate report.
limitations: No complete independently instrumented microphone-init, per-hop, answer-review or same-session final-score timing.
The cause of 8+1 outbound scheduling is not established by the traces; no fixed worker limit is asserted.
All measured voice records use Avatar + WebRTC. No pure WS or audio-only performance comparison is inferred.
First audible is the browser detector, not physical speaker output; response playback end and user comprehension are unmeasured.
